survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC) and therefore does not define a sampling frame, student-level analytic sample, or any survey-weight variables. The document is a governance and responsibilities mapping for adult skills system actors in the Slovak Republic, describing which levels of government design, fund, implement, and deliver policy areas (VET/HVET/CET/AE and ALMPs). As a result, plausible values (PV) and complex survey weighting procedures are not part of the methodology. For any future empirical analysis using ILSA microdata, analysts would need to apply the relevant ILSA sampling weights (and replicate weights if provided) to obtain population-representative estimates; however, this note itself provides no such estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a policy/governance country note and does not perform student-level assessment scoring or statistical modeling of cognitive outcomes. Because there is no PV-based achievement outcome (and no ILSA microdata analysis), plausible values are not applicable. Similarly, there is no missing-data handling described because no dataset with item responses or model-based estimation is analyzed in this note.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used as a country governance note for the Slovak Republic; no ILSA microdata sample is constructed or filtered.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note describes how the adult skills system in the Slovak Republic is governed across national, regional, and local levels. It reports the allocation of responsibilities for VET, HVET, CET, adult education (AE), and active labour market policies (ALMPs), including which level designs strategy and intelligence, funds, implements, and delivers services. The note specifies that education policies (VET/HVET/CET/AE) are designed and funded nationally, while implementation and delivery occur regionally and locally through secondary vocational schools, non-state schools, and adult education providers. For ALMPs, strategy and funding are national, with implementation via deconcentrated branch offices of the Central Office of Labour, Social Affairs and Family (PES), coordinating territorial offices that provide job mediation, counselling, and training. No assessment design, sampling, scaling, or performance benchmarks are evaluated because the document is not an empirical ILSA-based study.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse because the provided text is a governance/administrative description rather than an empirical study using ILSA or other large-scale assessment microdata. Consequently, there is no student sample, no statistical model, no ML pipeline, and no reported predictive performance to populate the ML-specific fields. The absence of PV and missing-data handling is by design: the note does not analyze cognitive test scores or estimation outputs.
